sessionStart.command: printf '%s\n' '{"additional_context":"## MANDATORY VIBEREVIEW SECURITY GATE\\n\\nConfigured project: Security TooL (security-tool, e00ccc4a-3cb0-4288-a2fa-57703efa93e8)\\n\\nFor any request with security impact, this is a hard pre-write gate. Do not create, edit, or patch code until steps 1-3 are complete:\\n\\nEvaluate every user prompt independently, including follow-up prompts in an existing IDE chat. If a follow-up changes auth, authorization, APIs/endpoints, webhooks, agents/tools, input/output handling, persistence, secrets, network calls, dependencies, infra, logging, monitoring, or any trust boundary, run this gate again and write a new event artifact. Reuse the same `chat_session_id` only to group that event under the existing scan; do not treat the prior event as coverage for the new prompt. Small changes are not exempt when they touch a security surface.\\n\\n1. Resolve the tenant/project with `vibereview_get_tenant_project` using project_id=\"e00ccc4a-3cb0-4288-a2fa-57703efa93e8\" or project_slug=\"security-tool\".\\n2. Fetch VibeReview guardrails with `vibereview_get_guardrails`, shortlist relevant guardrails, and preserve that shortlist.\\n3. Run PWNISMS threat modelling before implementation.\\n4. If the task adds/upgrades/imports any dependency, run the OSV.dev dependency scan (`.cursor/skills/osv-dependency-scan/SKILL.md`) before introducing the package. Do not block the flow: auto-substitute the recommended safe (fixed) version for any HIGH/CRITICAL finding (or a safe alternative / honest residual-risk note if no fix exists), re-scan it, flag what was avoided in the response, and record it in telemetry.\\n5. Implement secure code using the threat model, shortlisted guardrails, and the safe dependency versions chosen in step 4.\\n6. Write one structured JSON artifact under .vibereview/scans/ (see `schemas/scan-artifact-v1.json` in vibereview-kit). Include `chat_session_id`, stable `workflow_name`, and a prompt-specific `title`; reuse `chat_session_id` only for follow-up prompts in the same IDE chat. Prefer CLI `vibereview sync --file <path-to-this-json>` (or `npx -y @securityreviewai/vibereview sync --file <path-to-this-json>`) so only the current file is uploaded verbatim; use `--force` when retrying an empty/failed ingest for that same file. If using MCP: follow vibereview-sync **MCP completeness contract**—mirror every non-empty array via `vibereview_ctm_structured_patch_event` and/or `vibereview_ctm_structured_add_snippets` / `vibereview_ctm_structured_add_guardrails` / `vibereview_ctm_structured_add_owasp` with **no summarization**; chunk across multiple tool calls; only then `vibereview_ctm_structured_finalize` after row counts match the artifact.\\n\\nNo deferral. No code before guardrails. Vulnerable dependencies are auto-remediated to a safe version (not blocked) and flagged in telemetry. The main agent owns the final ingest. No local profiling.\\n"}'
